_note: The sector layer. Only what the first exhibit and its stat tiles actually render is authored here: current capacity, the 2030 forecasts, the build rate and the market size. The hyperscaler pledges and the IndiaAI outlay are in the brief and are deliberately not carried yet, because they have no exhibit, and this repository has already learned once what happens to a data file that renders on no page. Every figure is a research house projection or an industry estimate, so every source is SECONDARY and none may claim otherwise.

indiaAI._note: The government scheme that handed ten providers a deadline, which makes it the one place a reader can watch announcement and execution separate at provider level. The brief gives one provider's offer and a national installed total, not a per provider deployment table, so no per provider installed figure is recorded here and none is drawn. Status is what has been publicly reported about each, and five of the ten have nothing reported either way.

operatorReturns._note: The only primary figures on this page. Eight data centre operators, five Indian and three global, with return on capital and depreciation rate for three fiscal years, printed as a single table inside the prospectus industry report. NA in the source is carried as null and drawn as an absence, never as a zero.

claim.quote: Sify achieved ROCE of 9.88%, 6.75% and 7.92% in Fiscal 2023, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2025, respectively, which is significantly higher than its global peers.

issuerReason.quote: Sify's depreciation rose from INR 2,083.00 million in Fiscal 2023 to INR 3,268.16 million in Fiscal 2025, resulting in a depreciation rate of 10.33% in Fiscal 2025 the highest among its peers. This partly weighed on its ROCE.

source.label: Sify Infinit Spaces DRHP, peer benchmarking table inside the commissioned 1Lattice and Cushman and Wakefield industry report. Return on capital employed is EBIT over average capital employed, on the definition printed on the following page. Fiscal years are the Indian convention, ending 31 March. The two largest global names carry a footnote in the source marking a different reporting basis.
